findings.reason: the section must name `store_delivered_report` as the owner that carries `section_digests` into the stored record (or make the sidecar the predicate's store), else the migration path runs uncovered and every dispatch is refused.
findings.text: §16 writes the `section_digests` mapping through the composer into the review sidecar (`write_review_sidecar`, `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:848`, called at `reckon/crew/recovery.py:587`) but specifies the coverage predicate reads the section digests from the union of stored reviews enumerated by `list_plan_reviews` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:668`). Those are two different stores, and `store_delivered_report` builds its record from an explicit field dict that does not include `section_digests`, so the key never reaches the reader the predicate names — the predicate would find every outstanding section uncovered.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §16 hides the identity derivation, the per-section prose bucketing and the three recognised digest forms behind one private function, `_section_digests`, while explicitly holding the public `plan_fingerprint` interface fixed; §17 hides the raw-text span walk behind one public reader, `plan_headings`, over the private parser. §17 is net consolidation (nine private store helpers and `landed_section_ids` re-homed, no new scanner), which adds depth rather than surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16 leaves the owner of the `section_digests` record ambiguous between the review sidecar and the stored review record, and the reader it names (`list_plan_reviews`) is not the store the writer it names (`write_review_sidecar`) writes to.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23. §17 adds one public definition (`plan_headings`) and names its offset (the `landed_section_ids` move, family unchanged); §16 retires the public `legacy` parameter and adds none; §18 adds none and retires promotion's private reader. Net +1 public definition, each section accounting for its own surface; no CLI option, MCP view or refusal family is added (§16 explicitly reuses `plan-review-missing`).
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the three sections cite and I verified the existing machinery they extend: `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` and `structured_section_spans` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:44,94`), `section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:215,234`), `landed_section_ids` (`reckon/_store.py:1034`), the nine store helpers, `promotion._plan_remaining_sections` (`reckon/crew/promotion.py:7236`), `roadmap.implementable_sections` (`reckon/roadmap.py:106`), `doccheck._implementable_section_ids` (`reckon/doccheck.py:1014`), `list_plan_reviews`/`read_plan_review` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:668,618`), `interface_counts.read_trees`/`definitions`/`_staged_writes` (`reckon/interface_counts.py:47,65`), and the three section-spelling grammars (`routing._SECTION_IDENTITY`, `evidence._section_key`, `ledger.normalize_section`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every new layer is an extension of an existing owner rather than a parallel one: §18 extends `roadmap.implementable_sections` in place and deletes `promotion._plan_remaining_sections`; §17 rewrites heading walks onto the parser instead of adding a scanner; §16's coverage predicate is one module-private join over two existing readers with no walk of its own. The one thin public projection, `plan_headings`, states its reason (five cross-package consumers, so the private parser cannot be exposed directly).
